title: Marketplace metering, SKU & legal checklist — commerce copy + technical mapping (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working checklist and copyboard to align commerce metering, SKU mapping, and the minimal legal/compliance hooks required for cloud marketplace listings (AWS Marketplace, Azure Marketplace, GCP Marketplace). Goal: have a single canonical reference for engineering, legal, and GTM to avoid last-minute rework during listing submissions.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: listing SKU/entitlement design, metering events, short/long copy snippets for catalog pages, minimum legal statements required by platform vendors, launch acceptance gates.
- Audience: GTM product owners, billing engineers, platform integration PM, legal/compliance, partner ops.

High-level notes (working assumptions):
- We support two commerce models across vendors: 1) Metered usage (per-token/per-embedding unit) and 2) Subscription (monthly reserved capacity).
- SKU naming must be stable across vendors (internal SKU <-> marketplace SKU mapping).
- Trial entitlements must be enforced at the billing layer and mirrored in the product config (no soft trials that require manual toggle).

Quick checklist (technical & commercial gates):
1) SKU mapping CSV (engineering -> marketplace):
   - Required columns: internal_sku, marketplace_sku, sku_type (metered|subscription), unit_of_measure, unit_price_usd, billing_period, plan_name, free_trial_days, region_restrictions
   - TODO: generate canonical sample CSV and add to marketplace-scripts repo. (Linked: PR #42)
2) Metering events contract:
   - Define event_id names and attributes: token_generation, embedding_request, rerank_call, inference_p99_latency_ms.
   - Confirm event payload schema (timestamp, customer_id, sku, units_consumed, request_id).
   - Ensure idempotency key semantics for batched events.
3) Pricing & rounding rules:
   - Round up to nearest billing unit where applicable (e.g., embeddings billed per 1000 vectors).
   - Policy for fractional billing for subscription mid-cycle changes -> proration rules.
4) Trial enforcement flow:
   - Auto-grant trial via marketplace entitlement webhook.
   - Trial expiration: automatic downgrade to free tier or suspend access pending billing.
5) Reporting & reconciliation:
   - Daily usage exports in CSV/JSON for partner finance (UTC).
   - Reconciliation fields: invoice_id, marketplace_invoice_ref, usage_window_start/end.
6) Security & data residency callouts (per marketplace):
   - AWS: include data processing addendum statement + encryption at rest key options.
   - Azure: mention support for Azure regions + customer-managed keys.
   - GCP: include VPC-SC compatibility note if applicable.

Copyboard: product copy variants (do not finalize — these are suggestions)
- Short title (max 60 chars): Redwood Inference — Low-latency LLM inference platform
- Tagline (single line): Predictable inference performance: low latency, cost controls, and private deployment options.
- 1-line short description (for catalog listing): Production-grade LLM inference with per-token metering and reserved GPUs — deploy hosted, dedicated, or private.
- Long description (catalog detail):
  Redwood Inference provides a unified inference runtime that makes LLM-powered features predictable and economical at scale. Choose hosted API for instant access, reserved capacity for predictable throughput, or private deployment for regulated workloads. Features include intelligent batching and caching, transparent per-token cost analytics, and rollouts with canary/A-B strategies.

- Feature bullets (6):
  • Low-latency, GPU-optimized serving runtime
  • Metered usage + subscription pricing options
  • Autoscaling reserved pools and burst capacity
  • Prefix/KV caching and token-level cost dashboards
  • Canary rollouts, model version pinning, and automatic fallback
  • Integrations: KMS/HSM for key management, audit logs, SSO

Marketplace-specific short legal hooks (draft):
- Data Processing & Security: "We process customer inference requests to serve model outputs. Customer input data can be retained for up to 30 days for cache optimization unless disabled. Enterprise plans support data residency and KMS integrations."
- SLA & Support: "Enterprise / Dedicated plans include SLA-backed uptime and business-hour support; see our support SLA addendum for details."
- Billing & Refunds: "Usage aggregated daily; invoices issued monthly. Refunds processed per vendor terms; general refunds require approval from Redwood finance."
- Export compliance & sanctions: "Customers are responsible for export compliance; Redwood reserves the right to restrict access where required."

Platform submission checklist (per vendor) — minimum required artifacts:
- Listing copy (short + long + bullets) in vendor template.
- 2–3 high-res screenshots (console route, billing dashboard, metrics) with captions.
- SKU mapping CSV and sample metering events file.
- Legal boilerplate: DPA link, privacy policy version, support SLA doc link.
- Technical integration guide (1–2 page PDF): webhook endpoints, event schema, idempotency guidance.
- Contact person(s) for finance & legal (name, email).

Acceptance gates and signoffs (must be explicit before submission):
- Product: copy approved and screenshots final.
- Engineering: verified SKU mapping, test harness for metering events, reconciliation job running on staging.
- Legal/Privacy: DPA and marketplace-specific language approved.
- Finance: pricing table reconciled and internal SKUs mapped to GL codes.
- Sales/Ops: support runbook covering trial support & refunds.

Launch runway & rollout notes (operational):
- Prelaunch (2 weeks): staging listing published to vendor sandbox, end-to-end billing test (create trial user, consume tokens, verify invoice).
- Launch day: monitor reconciliation job, open dedicated Slack channel, standby finance contact for first 48 hours.
- Post-launch (30 days): weekly usage trend review and rate-limit/quotas adjustments based on early telemetry.

Open questions / TODOs (owner):
- Who will own marketplace refunds policy for metered invoices? (Owner: Finance)
- Finalize free_trial_days per vendor (AWS suggests 14; Azure allows 30). (Owner: Priya)
- Confirm whether marketplace will allow one-off promo SKUs for channel partners. (Owner: Partner Ops)
- Add sample CSV to marketplace-scripts repo and wire up validation CI. (Owner: Engineering / Ethan)

Appendix — sample SKU CSV header (canonical template):
internal_sku,marketplace_sku,sku_type,unit_of_measure,unit_price_usd,billing_period,plan_name,free_trial_days,region_restrictions,gl_code
RED-PRO-0001,aws-redwood-token-meter,metered,tokens,0.0005,monthly,Pro Token Pack,14,global,4100
RED-DED-100,azure-redwood-dedicated,subscription,seat,1200,monthly,Dedicated-32GB-GPU,0,us-east-1,4200

Appendix — common metering event types (short):
- token_generation: tokens_consumed
- embedding_vector: vectors_returned
- rerank: ranking_calls

Notes to reviewers: This is intentionally pragmatic and minimal — the marketplace teams will reject listings that are missing either the SKU mappings or the legal/DPAs. Keep comments inline and tag reviewers using @mentions in the Confluence PRD linked above.
